unpublished_reason: The speaker-vad-turn mode now has a fixture and was actually run: all 6 attribution assertions pass (the owner's words reach a public final, the next speaker's do not), but the mode's own verdict is still FAIL because the harness's self-imposed finish-recovery budget (finish to non-empty final within 1200 ms) is not met: 1652-1732 ms measured, essentially unchanged by this revision's fixes and inside the 1.1-2.4 s the shipped docs state. DEFAULT_DELIVERY.md requires the checked reports to be PASS, so the mode is recorded as waived and the package stays an unpublished candidate. The branch is also not yet merged to main.

product_changes: 1) Speaker diarization model and chain replaced: pyannote + WeSpeaker + PLDA/VBx (Community-1) removed without fallback, Sortformer-66M-4spk streaming model on CPU (ORT 1.16.3), 9.92 s chunk commits plus an optional in-chunk preview (scheduling.diarizationPreviewMs, default 5000). 2) Adjacent utterances of the same confirmed speaker are joined into one DiarizedUtterance; new sourceUtteranceIds field; speakerIndex=-1 never joins; speakerTurns unchanged. 3) Hotwords no longer swallow the text that follows: sherpa patches 0036 (a half-matched context prefix expires after 1 s of blanks, so a hypothesis parked on a partial match stops out-scoring real speech) and 0037 (a multi-token phrase's first-token bonus is capped at 1.0, so a boosted first character can no longer replace a real one); shared by both platforms, public API and hotword input format unchanged, the 1.0 preset pool and single-character hotwords behave as before. 4) Owner handoff: when no speaker-change point can be established the runtime now falls back to a conservative owner prefix instead of publishing a known mixture, and an utterance the streaming machine never confirmed must clear the measured floor 0.45 as well as the configured threshold; callback contract unchanged, a rejected utterance is still an empty final plus SPEAKER_VAD_REJECTED.

hotword_prefix_deletion_fix: PASS on host, partially verifiable on device. Root cause: the context bonus is granted on a phrase's first token with no evidence and scales with the caller score (3.0 for sysGeneralLexicon since 0.3.25), and a hypothesis parked on a partial match keeps that bonus while emitting blanks because the back-off only settles on a non-blank token, so silence out-scores real digits and the rest of the segment is deleted. Host regression on 500 aishell3 utterances with per-utterance hotwords at 3.0 plus the police preset pool: baseline CER 1.021% / hotword recall 97.25%, with 0036 only 1.039% / 97.58%, with 0036+0037 1.075% / 97.09% (1 of 619 hotword instances lost: 弗里曼). A two-character hotword can no longer force its first character at any score up to 100. Device, 7-case fixture: the customer's own 53-word list, the recording without that hotword, a single-character hotword and a two-character prefix are all correct; the constructed seven-character prefix probe went from losing all 11 digits to losing only the first 5. Patch 0037 could not be positively verified on device because the product layer fixes sysGeneralLexicon at 3.0 and this recording does not flip at 3.0; only the absence of regression was shown. See docs/asr/HOTWORD_PREFIX_DELETION_20261029.md.
speaker_turn_floor_caveat: The 0.45 floor rests on same-session enrolment (asr/tools/speaker/18_eval_short_segment_threshold.py: owner minimum 0.525/0.600/0.603/0.636 at 1.0/1.5/2.0/3.0 s versus non-target maximum 0.400/0.377/0.432/0.459, an empty band between 0.35 and 0.52), which flatters the owner side. Whether a cross-session enrolment rejects a genuine short owner utterance has to be re-measured with customer voiceprints before the floor is treated as validated for production.
